correctness.rationale: A diagonal one-parameter subgroup with weights 2^i has distinct induced weights on all Plucker coordinates. The dual variety is invariant. For any k-subset I, the hypotheses k>=2 and n-k>=2 allow construction of J with |I∩J|=k-2. The affine tangent cone to Gr(k,n) at e_J is wedge^{k-1}J wedge C^n, so its coordinate basis consists exactly of e_K with |K∩J|>=k-1. Therefore p_I vanishes on the full tangent space and H_I is tangent. Every ambient fixed point consequently lies in X^vee, and there are binomial(n,k) of them. Euler localization for algebraic C* actions gives the claimed ordinary Euler characteristic because X^vee is projective. The packaged checker exhaustively replays the subset/tangent criterion and weight separation for 4<=n<=14.

value.rationale: Projective duals of Grassmannians are classical discriminantal varieties whose degrees, singular loci, normality, and complement topology have substantial literature. The theorem gives a uniform global topological invariant for every nonprojective Plucker Grassmannian and reveals a sharp collapse: the singular dual, the smooth Grassmannian, and the entire ambient dual projective space all have the same Euler characteristic binomial(n,k). For k=2 this covers the projective Pfaffian rank loci that arise as duals of Grassmannians; for higher k it applies to generally complicated Grassmannian-dual hypersurfaces. The complement-Euler vanishing is a concrete global consequence and the proof explains the value through an exact tangent-coordinate mechanism rather than a small-case computation.
